title: Choose the numeric type
summary: A dtype tells TensorFlow how to store tensor values. Many model computations use floating-point numbers.
introduction: A dtype tells TensorFlow how to store tensor values. Many model computations use floating-point numbers. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A dtype tells TensorFlow how to store tensor values. Many model computations use floating-point numbers.

blocks.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([1, 2], dtype=tf.float32)
print(x.dtype.name)
blocks.title: Choose the numeric type

blocks.text: The output is float32. The explicit type controls the numeric representation.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Mixing incompatible numeric types can require an explicit cast.
For more detail later, use this [TensorFlow further reading](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/basics).
